attributes.title: Level 8

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use a base and an accent color to design a dirt tile asset, like this?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What colors might be used to create a dirt tile asset? 

❓ How can custom tile assets be created in MakeCode Arcade?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that tile assets can be created in the Assets menu. Alternatively, tile assets can be created within the tilemap editor in the My Tiles section. Tile assets in My Tiles can be edited, duplicated, and deleted. Remind the ninja that the size of all tile assets are 16x16, which cannot be changed.


💡 Remind the ninja that they can use the line tool to fill the bottom row of the tilemap with dirt tiles.
steps.instructions:
Begin the project by creating custom tile and tilemap assets!


Click the Assets menu along the top of the screen, then create a new tilemap asset. Resize the canvas to 35 x 16 and give the tilemap asset a descriptive name.


On the left side of the tilemap editor, select My Tiles, then create a new tile by clicking +. Design a dirt tile that uses a base color with another color that adds subtle accents to the tile. Give the tile asset a descriptive name.


Click Done, then fill the entire bottom row of the tilemap with dirt tiles.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use the line tool to draw a row of ground tiles just above the dirt tiles?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What colors might be used to add an outline and a highlight on the ground tile asset?

❓ Where should the ground tiles be placed on the tilemap asset?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that any tiles created in My Tiles will also appear in the Assets menu. They can be updated in both places as well.

💡 Remind the ninja that they should use a light color as the highlight and a slightly darker color as the outline in their ground tile. Prompt the ninja to consider what colors might match well with the ground/dirt tilemap theme.
steps.instructions:
Design a ground tile to be placed on top of the dirt tile.


Under My Tiles, select the dirt tile then click to duplicate the tile. Select the new tile, then click to edit it.


In the tile editor, use 2 different colors to add an outline and a highlight across the top row of the tile. This will create contrast to show the “top” of the ground, indicating where the sprite will stand. Give the tile asset a descriptive name.


Click Done, then place ground tiles along the bottom of the tilemap, just above the dirt tiles.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use the horizontal flip tool to create a right curved tile?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How might the curved tile assets be used on the tilemap?

❓ How might pixels be connected to create a curved edge in the tile asset?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja to use the documentation for help when creating a curved line in pixel art. Prompt the ninja to consider how they are connecting pixels, how many pixels are in each “step”, and to use the erase tool to remove any jaggies in the line. 

💡 The curved tile assets will be used to create hills on the tilemap. A curved tile asset in each direction is needed to create a full “bump”, which will act as an obstacle for a sprite.
steps.instructions:
Design 2 curved tile assets to add hills to the tilemap!


Under My Tiles, select the ground tile then click to duplicate the tile. Select the new tile, then click to edit it.


In the tile editor, use the erase tool to remove pixels from the top left half of the image. Then, use the outer outline color to draw a curved line from the top right corner of the canvas, to the bottom left. Connect the pixels diagonally and remove any jaggies. 


Use the inner highlight color to add an inner curved line underneath the shadow. Then, update any other pixels to polish the asset. Give the tile asset a descriptive name.


Click Done, then duplicate the left curved tile. Flip the new tile horizontally so that it curves to the right instead. Give the tile asset a descriptive name.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you create and add corner tiles to smooth the transition between curved and flat top ground tiles, like this?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Where might the curved tile assets be placed on the tilemap? What should be placed between them?

❓ Why might a corner tile be needed to smooth the transition between curved and flat top ground tiles?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Prompt the ninja to consider where to add hills to the tilemap. They should space them out in a strategic way, so that the sprite has enough room to move between them. Encourage the ninja to create hills of varying heights and widths to create an engaging tilemap scene. Remind the ninja that ground and dirt tiles should be used to fill in the space between curved tiles, to create cohesive terrain.

💡 Explain to the ninja that corner tiles may be needed to fill in gaps between tiles with different types of lines. Prompt the ninja to explore MakeCode’s existing tiles in the gallery to notice how they have designed corner tiles to create cohesive platforms. 

💡 In this tilemap, the corner tile asset should include the dirt tile, with just a few pixels in the corner that smooth the transition between the curved and flat top ground tile lines.
steps.instructions:
Use the curved tiles to create uneven terrain on the tilemap!


In the tilemap editor, add several left and right curved tiles onto the ground. Fill the space between the tiles using ground and dirt tiles. 


Create hills of different heights and widths by placing curved tiles further away from each other or stacked diagonally as a staircase. Remove existing layers of the tilemaps to create dips in the ground.


Notice how the curved tile transitions into the flat top of the ground tile. Create and add corner tiles, as needed, to form a smooth line between the 2 types of tiles.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you remove a few pixels from the top and bottom left corners of the floating platform tile to create a rounded, half circle shape, like this?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why might floating platform tiles be useful in this project?

❓ How should the floating platform tile asset be different than the curved tile asset?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that they are creating a 2D tilemap that should include a variety of platforms in it. In this project, the sprite’s velocity and acceleration will be set so that it can jump and climb up to the different platforms on the tilemap.

💡 Point out to the ninja that the floating platform tile asset should fill most of the canvas, whereas the curved tile asset should only take up about half of the space. The ninja should only remove pixels from the top and bottom corners of one side of the floating platform tile asset, leaving the pixels in the middle that touch the edge of the canvas to create a rounded, half circle shape.
steps.instructions:
Design floating platform tiles to add to the tilemap!


In My Tiles, duplicate the ground tile then open the new tile to edit it.


Use the erase tool to remove a few pixels from the top left and bottom left corners of the image. Make sure the pixels in each corner are connected diagonally to create a rounded, half circle shape on the left side of the image. Give the tile asset a descriptive name.


Click Done, then duplicate the left floating platform tile. Flip the new tile so that its right edge is rounded instead. Give the tile asset a descriptive name.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you turn the walls on for each ground and floating platform tile on the tilemap?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Where might floating platform tiles be placed on the tilemap?

❓ What tool(s) can be used to add walls to the tiles on the tilemap?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Prompt the ninja to notice where hills have been added on the ground terrain of the tilemap and where it might make sense to add floating platforms in the space above. Encourage the ninja to create platforms of varying widths by placing smaller and larger amounts of ground tiles between the floating platform tiles.

💡 Remind the ninja that they can select both the fill tool and the draw walls tool to add walls to a large section of tiles on the tilemap. The erase and draw walls tools can be used together to remove any accidental walls.



💡 Point out to the ninja that because tile assets are 16x16 squares, portions of the curved tile assets act as walls, even though they appear to be transparent. Once the project is built and run, the sprite will be able to stand on these pixels because they are walls, sometimes giving the effect that the sprite is “standing on air”.
steps.instructions:
Add the floating platform tiles to the tilemap!


In the tilemap editor, add several left and right floating platform tiles, with ground tiles in between, in the empty space above the existing ground tiles. 


Create platforms of different widths by placing the left and right floating platform tiles further away from each other. Place platforms in different rows and columns in the empty space, positioning them strategically on the tilemap.


Once the floating platform tiles have been added, use the draw walls and fill tools to turn the walls on for every tile placed on the tilemap.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you place the ladder tiles to the left or right of each floating platform so the sprite can use them to reach each floating platform?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What might be added to the ladder tile to show the rungs of the ladder with a highlight underneath?

❓ Where might ladder tiles be placed on the tilemap?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Prompt the ninja to consider what colors might be used to make the ladder tiles stand out on the tilemap. Have the ninja use a darker color as the base of the ladder’s rungs, and a lighter color for the highlight to create a sharp contrast on the tilemap.

💡 Explain to the ninja that the ladder tiles will be used for the sprite to climb up onto the floating platforms. As a result, ladders should be placed to the right or left of floating platform tiles so that the sprite can enter from one side.
steps.instructions:
Design a ladder tile to allow the sprite to reach the floating platforms.


Create a new tile in My Tiles. Use a base color to design a ladder tile. Use a different highlight color above or below each of the ladder’s rungs to create a contrast in the tile image. Give the tile asset a descriptive name.


In the tilemap editor, stack ladder tiles vertically to connect them from the ground (or a floating platform) to the top of the tilemap. Place the ladders strategically, so that the sprite will be able to climb the ladders in order to reach each floating platform.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you select a background image and update the colors to match the theme of the tilemap?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What background image might be used in this project?

❓ How might the background image be modified to match the theme of the tilemap


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that the background image will appear behind the tilemap asset on screen. As a result, the image should match the theme of the tilemap. Encourage the ninja to change the colors of the background image asset to better align it with the tilemap.
steps.instructions:
Add a background image and tilemap to the project!


Create a background image asset in the Assets menu. Select an image that will appear behind the tilemap in the project. Give the image asset a descriptive name.


Return to the JavaScript editor, then add a // project start comment. Below, add code to display the background image and tilemap assets on screen.


Click ▶ to see the background image and tilemap on screen.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you open the tilemap asset to find the coordinates to place the Player sprite on?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Where should the Player sprite be placed on the tilemap?

❓ Why should the Player sprite only be able to move horizontally on screen?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 The Player sprite should be placed on the bottom left ground tile on the tilemap. Prompt the ninja to open the tilemap asset to find the coordinates of this tile.

💡 Remind the ninja that they’ve created a 2D tilemap, meaning that the user’s perspective is from the side. This means that the Player sprite requires velocity and acceleration to control its vertical movement.
steps.instructions:
Add a Player sprite to explore the tilemap!


Create a Player sprite in the Assets menu by drawing an image or selecting one from the gallery. Give the image asset a descriptive name.


Return to the JavaScript editor, then add the Player sprite that is placed on the bottom left ground tile on the tilemap. Set the camera to follow the Player sprite and allow it to only move horizontally with buttons.


Click ▶ to test the Player sprite’s code.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you set the Player sprite’s y-velocity to a small, negative value so that it is not able to reach the floating platforms when it jumps?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What function is needed to check if the Player sprite is standing on a wall tile, before it jumps in the air?

❓ What might the Player sprite’s y-velocity be set to, so that it’s able to jump over hills on the ground terrain, but is unable to reach the floating platforms?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Prompt the ninja to use the documentation for help with coding the Player sprite to jump only when standing on top of a wall tile.

💡 The ninja should set the Player sprite’s y-velocity to a small, negative value so that it moves up on the screen, but not so high that it can reach the floating platforms.
steps.instructions:
Allow the Player sprite to jump on screen to reach the ladders!


Add code to set the Player sprite’s y-acceleration to 500. Then, add a  // project events comment  with code that allows the Player sprite to jump when standing on a wall tile when the A button is pressed.


Click ▶ to test the Player sprite’s jumping ability. Tinker with the y-velocity value so that the sprite is able to jump over the hills, but not reach the floating platforms.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you set the tileKindAt function’s parameters to TileDirection.Center and the ladder tile asset?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What does the tileKindAt function do? What is it being used for?

❓ What will happen when the Player sprite overlaps a ladder tile?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 The tileKindAt function checks if a tile image matches the tile (if any) next to a sprite. In this example, the function is checking to see if there is a ladder tile at the center of the Player sprite. This enables the sprite’s movement to only change when it is directly on a ladder tile, not overlapping it slightly.

💡 When the Player sprite overlaps a ladder tile, if there is a ladder tile at its center, the sprite will be able to move in all 4 directions and its y-acceleration will be set to 0. Else, the sprite will only be able to move horizontally and its y-acceleration will be reset to 500. This will allow the Player sprite to climb up and down ladders only if there is a ladder tile at its center.
steps.instructions:
Allow the Player sprite to climb up and down the ladders on the tilemap!


Use an onOverlapTile event to make something happen when the Player sprite overlaps a ladder tile.


Add an if/else conditional inside the event, then open Scene and drag [tile to (direction) of (mySprite) is (tile)] into the parentheses of the if condition. Notice how the code block turns into JavaScript text:


mySprite.tileKindAt(TileDirection.Left,

img` `)


The tileKindAt function checks if a tile image matches the tile (if any) next to a sprite. It takes 2 parameters: a direction and a tile image. Check if the tile at the center of the Player sprite is a ladder tile.


If the condition is true, set the sprite to move in all 4 directions and set its y-acceleration to 0. Else, set the sprite to only move horizontally and reset its y-acceleration to 500. 


Click ▶ to test what happens when the Player sprite climbs up and down the ladders!

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use the marquee, paint, and erase tools to show the sprite climbing up and down the ladders across 2 or 3 frames?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What animation asset should be used to show the Player sprite climbing up and down the ladders?

❓ What happens when the up and down buttons are pressed?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 If the ninja selected its Player sprite image from the gallery, they can use an existing MakeCode animation asset for the climbing animation. If there is not a matching animation, they can use additional frames from the gallery to give the appearance of the sprite climbing. If the ninja created their own Player sprite image, prompt them to consider what image frames are needed to create a climbing animation asset for the Player sprite.

💡 When the up and down buttons are pressed, if there is a ladder tile at the Player sprite’s center, the climbAnim animation asset will run.
steps.instructions:
Create a climbing animation asset for the Player sprite!


Create a climbAnim animation asset in the Assets menu. Draw or select an image from the gallery that shows the Player sprite’s back in the first frame. Add additional frames to show the sprite climbing up and down the ladders.


Return to the JavaScript editor and create an up button pressed event. Add an if conditional inside the event, then open Scene and drag [tile to (direction) of (mySprite) is (tile)] into the parentheses of the if condition. 


Use the dot operator to check for the tile at the center of the sprite. Set the tile parameter to the ladder tile asset. If the ladder tile is at the center of the sprite, set the sprite’s climbing animation to run.


Duplicate the up button pressed event to set the code to also run when the down button is pressed.


Click ▶ to test the Player sprite’s climbing animation.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you add on button pressed events for the left and right buttons so that the sprite animation updates to the correct direction?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What animation asset should be used to show the Player sprite walking left and right on the tilemap?

❓ What happens when the left and right buttons are pressed?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 If the ninja selected its Player sprite image from the gallery, they can use an existing MakeCode animation asset for the walking animation. If there is not a matching animation, they can use additional frames from the gallery to give the appearance of the sprite walking. If the ninja created their own Player sprite image, prompt them to consider what image frames are needed to create walking animation assets for the Player sprite.

💡 When the left and right buttons are pressed, the runImageAnimation function will run, showing the walkingLeftAnim or walkingRightAnim animation assets.
steps.instructions:
Create a walking animation asset for the Player sprite!


Create a walkingLeftAnim animation asset in the Assets menu. Draw or select an image from the gallery that shows the Player sprite walking left in the first frame.


Duplicate the walkingLeftAnim animation asset, then use the horizontal flip tool to create a walkingRightAnim animation asset.


Return to the JavaScript editor and code the Player sprite’s animation to change on left and right button pressed events. Update the runImageAnimation parameters accordingly.


Click ▶ to test the Player sprite’s walking animation.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use an on anyButton released event to stop all animation?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why should all animations stop when the A button is pressed and when any button is released?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Animations should stop when the A button is pressed and when any button is released to prevent the Player sprite from appearing like it’s walking, even when it’s climbing a ladder or jumping in the air.
steps.instructions:
Oh no! The Player sprite looks like it’s walking, even when it’s not!


Add code to stop all animation when the A button is pressed, above the if conditional. 


Then, create an event that stops all animation from running when any button is released.


Click ▶ to test out the animation code and play the completed project!

subgroups.title: Hills and Ladders
subgroups.introduction: Design custom tiles to create unique platforms and terrain in a 2D platformer tilemap!

validationItems.text: Create 3 custom tile assets to create a 2D tilemap with original ground terrain, floating platform, and ladder tiles.
Allow the Player sprite to move up and down ladder tiles.
Use a climbing animation while the Player sprite is moving up or down a ladder tile.
Use a walking animation when the Player sprite is walking left or right.
Stop all animations when any button is released.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 8 of Brown Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about creating original tile assets to build unique tilemaps. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 8:

badges.title: Mapping It Out
badges.description: Use a variety of pixel art techniques to create original tile assets that can be used for top-down or 2D tilemaps.

badges.title: A Whole New World
badges.description: Create original tile assets, including ground terrain and floating platform tiles, that can be used to design a 2D tilemap.

badges.title: Open Concept
badges.description: Create original tile assets that can be combined in a variety of ways to design structures that span multiple tiles.

badges.title: Changing It Up
badges.description: Change a sprite’s movement ability based on its location in relation to a specific tile kind.
